contractChanges.HOME-001: Replaces the owner front door with a public product landing at /: hero, invitee, host, essentials, alternative-request and self-hosting sections and a closing call, linking to /docs/install, /docs, the source repository and /signin. It keeps the deployment-configured description (now the footer's tagline) and owner identity (now optional in the public deployment configuration and named in the footer only when configured; a new install configures none), the link to the host's public booking profile when one exists (shown ahead of the headline) and the configurable Powered by Dial credit, and drops the earlier not-a-vendor-marketing-page wording. A deployment without a host profile now renders the landing instead of the recovery page. Security consequences: none relaxed. The page stays sessionless and read-only, reads only the public host profile it read before, sets no cookie, writes nothing to browser storage (a document opened on the public site turns off the router’s session-stored scroll positions, and links between the public site and the other surfaces load a new document), uses no tracking, and loads only same-origin resources, with a self-hosted font and inline decorative drawings. The shared Dial mark and favicon change on every surface; no migration is required.
contractChanges.EVENT-006: Adds explicit request-only publication for a draft or disabled event with a saved valid host profile/timezone, alternative requests enabled and verified transactional mail. No open availability window, calendar or conferencing readiness is required for receiving proposals, but no availability, bookable slot or booking creation is permitted. Normal automatic-booking publication retains all prior readiness checks and clears request-only mode only after success. Event configuration writes atomically advance the persisted revision even under a stalled or backwards clock; date override writes revise the parent in the same transaction. Checked publication, request-only opening and in-flight copy reports reject stale configuration without overwriting newer edits. No migration is required for this concurrency correction. Calendar is now optional for fixed-link, phone and in-person automatic booking. Saved availability and mail remain required; connected calendars must pass live checks and Google Meet still requires conferencing capability. Absence never masks a broken connection. Publishing is the explicit action enabling real bookings; setup and publication disclose that disconnected events do not check external calendar conflicts. No additional opt-in preference or migration is introduced for this notice.
contractChanges.PUBLIC-001: Replaces simultaneous display of every weekly slot with a day-first picker: each invitee-zone date appears once, every valid weekly slot remains reachable by selecting its day, and only the selected day's times appear. The first valid day opens initially. Up to five suggested times precede other times on that day, using the native AVAIL-007 ranking and reasons for those valid slots. Bounded week navigation and all event facts remain required.
contractChanges.AVAIL-005: The selected-day time group names its invitee zone once while each time retains a UTC offset, distinguishing repeated wall-clock times. Other invitee-facing times retain zone and offset. In the selected-day picker only, host time appears when zones differ and includes its date when dates differ. Details and confirmation retain host-local time even when zones match, including BOOK-005's both-zone receipt requirement. Browser-local zone resolution, UTC slot fetching, no pre-interaction visitor data, confirmed zone storage and all privacy guarantees remain unchanged.
contractChanges.AUTH-002: The consumed alternative-request review nonce also grants a read-only acknowledgement-state receipt for its original request and public event, including after nonce expiry, preserving existing consumed-nonce replay lifetime. The response exposes only queued, sent or failed, reports sent only after the invitee acknowledgement command succeeded, is unavailable for unavailable or erased requests/events, and grants no new mutation or other data access. Existing nonce issuance, confirmation expiry, single-use and event-binding guarantees remain.
contractChanges.DATA-001: Adopts Base portability JSON-lines archives and shared guarded CLI. Retains durable owner/native identities, exact schema/migration proof, original R2 assets, rich credential redaction and historical-effect retirement. Enforces separately supplied SESSION_SECRET continuity. Restores into an empty local destination with atomic D1 commit and owned-object cleanup. Legacy v2 transport and remote archive commands are retired; restore legacy files with their original revision before upgrading/exporting. No remote support is claimed. Adds native-owner authenticated hosted export through published Base HTTP primitives, durable source admission and expiring maintenance; schema proof and canonical policy are shared with local restoration. All FILES bytes and metadata travel; queue/alarm execution authority does not. Remote restore remains unavailable. No live account qualification is claimed. Installed migration ledgers must match source names and any recorded hashes/applied states. Hosted-to-local qualification covers the published importSql migration path and independent published CLI export, preserving destination installer records.
contractChanges.BASE-DATA-001: Corrects the restore command to pnpm run import so the package script is invoked rather than pnpm’s dependency importer. DATA-001 states the credential/live-authority exceptions and whole-archive canonicalization; empty-destination refusal and export/import/export equivalence remain required.
contractChanges.DOCS-001: Adds first-party public documentation at /docs and /docs/<slug>, rendered at build time from the Markdown files docs/site.json publishes, with every other root or docs Markdown file listed there as GitHub-only. The Markdown and highlighting libraries are development dependencies that run only inside Vite and never reach the Worker or browser bundles, which the build output check enforces. The new sessionless public path is GET-only and serves a static build artifact: it reads no booking, invitee, host-profile or operator record or session, sets no cookie, loads only same-origin resources and answers unknown, miscased or nested slugs with the existing 404 page. /docs and /docs/ are declared in deploy.publicPaths, so the Worker applies the same shared atomic public admission budget to them as to other public documents. Raw HTML in a page fails the build rather than being rendered, links pass a scheme allowlist and images are restricted to docs/media/. No existing protection is relaxed and no migration is required.
contractChanges.AUTH-001: Extends the declared native authentication public surface with AUTH-006 first-owner capability admission. Other private mutation and ownership gates remain required.
contractChanges.AUTH-006: Adds optional managed signed admission through exact Base owner-claim and operator-auth, with no-write invalid claims and atomic permanent singleton custody. Local setup-token admission is retained only without managed claim bindings.
contractChanges.EDITOR-001: Adds optional owner-authorized Base editor in the native app shell, private short-lived configuration, bounded expiry/revocation, immediate logout removal and exact trusted management framing.
contractChanges.DATA-003: Adds synthetic-only saved-data move-in: zero-write preview, reviewed inert D1 batches, resume, conflict-preserving undo, retained-source privacy erasure, imported slot occupancy and unsent manage capabilities. Newly planned imported creations record the authenticated importing operator and imported start in native history. For these creations only, BOOK-010's time is the immutable reviewed snapshot as-of instant, labelled as effective snapshot time rather than application wall-clock time; booking and original occurrence retain source creation time. OPER-004 exposes that distinction and native history. Already-reviewed plans retain their exact custody. Later native actions keep actual action times; imported operator cancellation sends one ordinary invitee cancellation mail and preserves the source calendar entry. Location reports account for the source row replaced by an owner choice, describe its selected type/value, and count no synthetic location as a source row. Preview captures its as-of instant on upload rather than file selection; repeated previews and choice changes within one upload preserve its initial instant, while reselecting files begins a fresh review. Apply and stored-job resume preserve the exact reviewed instant. Each source booking receives separate 256-bit native CSPRNG input in a server-issued, signed, owner/native-session/source/time-bound upload identity before review. Its 30-minute lifetime and atomic undo-generation fence prevent reuse for a new application. Binding the native session also prevents a pre-undo upload identity regaining authority after archive restore resets import history while preserving the operator and SESSION_SECRET. A runtime restart preserving the session retains the pending review; a new sign-in requires a fresh upload review. Existing persisted jobs resume from their exact plan under current native authentication. Native session authority, full reviewed fingerprints, exact target comparisons, native undo mutation detection and persisted-plan resume remain unchanged; the identity and raw manage capabilities never enter downloadable reports or archives. Missing imported private locations offer an event-editor recovery in setup and the operator app without bypassing normal publication readiness. The product declares no incumbent replacement: validation remains synthetic-only and a real account export has not been supplied.
contractChanges.OPER-005: First-run completion permits published fixed-location schedule-only booking; checklist labels Calendar optional while showing unhealthy connected calendars as outstanding.
contractChanges.PROFILE-003: Implements current-host avatar upload, replace and removal, generated private R2 storage, signature/type/size validation, session-gated mutations, same-origin inline current-avatar delivery, and original-byte archive preservation. No deployed-media acceptance is claimed.
contractChanges.OPER-003: Implements combinable URL-persisted booking filters and literal full Unicode case-insensitive substring search. Native local 100000-booking measurements are recorded with p50, p95 and observed maxima in ACCEPTANCE.md; local results do not establish production capacity or an every-request latency guarantee.
contractChanges.CUSTOM-001: Adds operator-defined private annotations on event types, bookings and availability requests through declared static contributions and slots. Four field types and manifest-estimated definition limits use extension-owned sidecars; invitee questions retain EVENT-003.
contractChanges.CUSTOM-002: Requires native session validation, private projections, original annotation archive restoration and boundary rejection of invalid references/types/choices. Complete erasure acceptance remains separately scoped in ACCEPTANCE.md.
contractChanges.AVAIL-004: With no connected calendar use saved schedule and persisted bookings without provider I/O. Any configured unhealthy, revoked or incomplete connection retains fail-closed reads; Google Meet cannot offer slots without its provider.
contractChanges.BOOK-001: Final confirmation always rechecks saved schedule and persisted bookings; the fresh provider read applies when connected. Atomic cross-event occupancy and nonce idempotency are preserved.
contractChanges.CAL-001: Explicitly absent or disconnected calendars permit fixed-location booking. Existing provider-managed bookings retain obligations and cannot silently abandon managed events during reschedule.
contractChanges.CAL-003: Migration 0042 persists calendar applicability separately from provider outcome; absent-calendar bookings expose not_required, create no calendar commands and never claim succeeded. Existing rows default to provider-required. Creation, reschedule, cancellation, mail, reminders and erasure honor applicability.
contractChanges.NOTIFY-006: Sender verification requires the sending API key and address, not the optional delivery-event verification key. Unchecked readiness has no missing-input diagnosis. Settings distinguishes sender readiness from event tracking; unsigned callbacks remain refused with or without a configured key.

agentUpdateInstructions:
Read this release record’s contractChanges and migrations before updating. Preserve authored data, existing local or deployed state, native operator and setup identities, durable setup-completion markers, and every already-applied migration byte. Back up before upgrading; apply only new SQL in filename order through the owner-authorized deployment procedure in OPERATIONS.md. Do not reset or replace state to upgrade. Migration 0016 revokes legacy sessions and consumes old sign-in links, so operators need fresh links after upgrade.

For a portable local backup, stop dev or preview and export to a new path: pnpm exec rer export --output exports/NAME.rer. Keep the archive and original private settings securely outside local state. Restore only into an empty destination: restore the original settings, including the same private SESSION_SECRET, before pnpm exec rer import --input exports/NAME.rer --yes; do not run setup first. The archive omits SESSION_SECRET and carries only its non-secret continuity digest needed for retry and erasure guards. Import preserves native owner identity and durable setup completion, but excludes credentials, sessions, links, and provider authority. Then run pnpm exec rer setup --owner-email ORIGINAL_OWNER_EMAIL, start pnpm exec rer dev, and follow the newest message in the printed loopback outbox; no external email is sent. If D1/R2 restore is interrupted, leave the destination unpublished and recover after inspection or use another empty destination.

pnpm exec rer deploy --dry-run performs local validation and makes no provider requests. For an owner-account deployment, follow OPERATIONS.md and its account and secret requirements. The retained owner-owned controller, deploy-kit, and root operations remain an explicit exception outside current RER retirement, including their native-bootstrap-aware health path. Current public RER deploy health still requires SETUP_TOKEN after bootstrap consumption, so keep it configured. No live provider, deployment, or release acceptance is claimed.

HOME-001: owner in src/ext/public-config.ts is now optional and the landing footer names it only when present; an install still carrying the earlier placeholder owner name (Your business) should set its real name or remove the owner entry.
